name: ZeroSignalEscrow

methods.name: init
methods.desc:
Post-create initialization. Opts the escrow's account into the
configured USDC asset so it can hold and disburse USDC at settle time.
The bootstrap funds 0.1 ALGO of ASA-MBR + 1 × min-fee on the app
address before calling this. Single-shot — second call reverts on the
`app already opted into USDC` assertion.

methods.name: createOperator

args.name: mbrPayment
args.desc: Funds the operator's box MBR. sender == Txn.sender, receiver == app, amount == mbrForOperator().

args.name: usdcStake
args.desc: Escrows the base operator stake in USDC. sender == Txn.sender, assetReceiver == app, xferAsset == usdcAssetId, assetAmount == requiredOperatorStakeUsdc() (== operatorStakeUsd6, since USDC is 6-decimal). When the configured stake is 0 (e.g. localnet/testnet) registration is free and this leg is ignored — callers still pass a dummy 0-amount axfer to keep the group shape uniform.

args.name: nfdAppId
args.desc: Optional NFD app id for this operator's published name; 0 if unset.

methods.desc:
Allocates a fresh operator id and creates the operator's box.
Txn.sender becomes the registered owner account — the only account
that can later call updateOperator / unregisterOperator / createNode
for this id. Returns the assigned id; off-chain composers parse it
from the method-result return so they can persist the id alongside
their config. The operator has no nodes until createNode is called, so
a freshly-created operator is not yet reachable or openable.

methods.name: updateOperator

args.name: operatorId
args.desc: The operator id to update.

args.name: operatorOwner
args.desc: The new owner account (may equal the current one if only nfd is rotating).

args.name: nfdAppId
args.desc: The new NFD app id (0 to clear).

methods.desc:
Rotates an operator's owner and/or NFD app id. Only the currently
registered owner account can call this — today's owner signs the txn
naming tomorrow's owner. The id, status, node counters, and all
rolled-up metrics carry forward unchanged (in-place write). Node-level
fields (signing key, URL) rotate via updateNode / updateNodeUrl instead.

methods.name: reinstateOperator

args.name: operatorId
args.desc: The operator id to reinstate.

methods.desc:
Clears the evicted tombstone, returning the operator to ACTIVE.
Admin-only — eviction is now an admin moderation action, so only an
admin can undo it (e.g. a mistaken eviction). Already-slashed USDC stays
with the treasury; this does not restore any stake. ids, nodes, and
metrics survive eviction, so a reinstated operator picks up exactly where
it left off.

methods.name: createNode

args.name: mbrPayment
args.desc: Funds the node's box MBR. sender == Txn.sender, receiver == app, amount == mbrForNode().

args.name: usdcStake
args.desc: Escrows this node's incremental stake in USDC. sender == Txn.sender, assetReceiver == app, xferAsset == usdcAssetId, assetAmount == requiredNodeStakeUsdc(operatorId) — 0 for the operator's first node (covered by the base operator stake), else nodeStakeUsd6 (== micro-USDC). A 0-amount transfer is still required so the group shape is uniform.

args.name: operatorId
args.desc: The operator that will own this node.

args.name: signing
args.desc: The node's signing account (hot key) used to sign tickets / receipts and authorize open/settle.

args.name: baseUrl
args.desc: The node's HTTP base URL (max 248 bytes).

returns.desc: The newly-assigned node id (unique within the operator).

methods.desc:
Creates a new node box under `operatorId` and returns its node id.
Only the operator's owner may call this, and only while the operator
is ACTIVE. The MBR payment funds the node box.

methods.name: updateNode

args.name: operatorId
args.desc: The owning operator id.

args.name: nodeId
args.desc: The node id to update.

args.name: signing
args.desc: The new node signing account.

args.name: baseUrl
args.desc: The new HTTP base URL (max 248 bytes).

methods.desc:
Rotates a node's signing key and/or base URL. Only the operator's owner
may call this, while the operator is ACTIVE. The node's metrics carry
forward unchanged (in-place write) so a node can't reset its reliability
score by rotating its signing key.

methods.name: updateNodeUrl

args.name: operatorId
args.desc: The owning operator id.

args.name: nodeId
args.desc: The node id to update.

args.name: baseUrl
args.desc: The new HTTP base URL (max 248 bytes).

methods.desc:
Updates only a node's base URL. Callable by the operator's owner OR
the node's current signing account (mirrors the convenience the old
updateOperatorUrl gave the hot key), while the operator is ACTIVE.

methods.name: setNodeStaging

args.name: operatorId
args.desc: The owning operator id.

args.name: nodeId
args.desc: The node id to update.

args.name: staging
args.desc:
True to mark the node as staging, false (the
createNode default) for production.

methods.desc:
Sets a node's `staging` flag. A staging node still advertises on-chain but
is meant to be held out of normal routing/selection, so an operator can
bring a node up for testing without serving production traffic. Callable
by the operator's owner OR the node's current signing account (mirrors
updateNodeUrl), while the operator is ACTIVE. The node's metrics and other
fields carry forward unchanged.

methods.name: unregisterNode

args.name: operatorId
args.desc: The owning operator id.

args.name: nodeId
args.desc: The node id to remove.

methods.desc:
Deletes a node box and refunds its MBR (ALGO) plus its incremental USDC
stake to the owner. Only the operator's owner may call this. Decrements
the operator's liveNodeCount — all nodes must be removed before
unregisterOperator can run. Works regardless of operator status (you must
be able to tear down an evicted operator's nodes) and is not gated on
`paused` (teardown / MBR reclaim stays available during a halt).

The USDC refund is clamped to the operator's remaining escrowed total, so
a prior eviction slash (which reduced usdcEscrowed below the sum of node
increments) can never over-refund — the owner can reclaim at most what is
actually still escrowed.

methods.name: unregisterOperator

args.name: operatorId
args.desc: The operator id to remove.

methods.desc:
Voluntarily removes an operator and refunds its box MBR to the owner.
All node boxes must be torn down first (unregisterNode) — asserted via
liveNodeCount — since the contract can't delete an unbounded number of
boxes in one call.

methods.name: evictOperator

args.name: operatorId
args.desc: The operator id to evict.

args.name: slashBps
args.desc:
Basis points (0..BPS_DENOMINATOR) of the
operator's current usdcEscrowed to slash. 0 evicts without slashing.

args.name: reason
args.desc:
Free-form moderation note (UTF-8, ≤ 1024 bytes) —
the admin's stated cause for the eviction. When a slash occurs it
rides as the `note` on the USDC transfer to the treasury, so the
reason is permanently recorded on-chain against the slashed funds.
Has no on-chain effect when the resulting slash is 0 (no transfer to
annotate); pass empty bytes in that case.

methods.desc:
Admin-only SOFT eviction with slashing — the protocol moderation lever
for a misbehaving operator. Marks the operator EVICTED (a tombstone: the
operator box and all its node boxes persist and in-flight tickets still
settle, but discovery hides it and open() reverts against its nodes) and
slashes `slashBps` basis points of its currently-escrowed USDC stake.

Slashed USDC is sent to the protocol treasury directly — it is never
burned. The non-slashed remainder stays escrowed on the operator box and
is reclaimable by the owner via unregister (clamped so a slash can never be
undone by per-node refunds). Reinstatement back to ACTIVE is a separate
admin action (reinstateOperator); it does not restore slashed stake.

methods.name: depositMbr

args.name: payment
args.desc: ALGO funding the deposit. sender == caller, receiver == app, amount > 0.

methods.desc:
Payer funds (or tops up) their prepaid ticket-MBR pool. The first call is
an OptIn that allocates the payer's local state — the local-schema MBR is
locked in the PAYER's own account by the opt-in itself, it is NOT sent
here; later calls are NoOp top-ups. The accompanying ALGO payment goes to
the app and raises both app free balance (which backs ticket boxes) and
the payer's credited algoBalance. open() draws box-MBR headroom against
this balance instead of a per-turn payer-signed feePayment leg.

methods.name: withdrawMbr

args.name: amount
args.desc: microALGO to withdraw. Must be <= available.

methods.desc:
Payer reclaims unreserved ALGO from their pool. available = algoBalance −
openTickets * ticketMbrOnly(); the reserved part backs live ticket boxes
(including frozen) and is locked until those boxes are deleted. Sends
`amount` back via inner payment (caller sizes the outer fee to cover the
1 inner). Does not change opt-in status or openTickets.

methods.name: closeDeposit
methods.desc:
Payer closes their pool entirely and opts out. Reverts while any ticket
box (including frozen) is still live (openTickets != 0). Inner-refunds the
remaining algoBalance; the CloseOut then returns the local-schema MBR to
the payer natively (no inner needed for it). Caller sizes the outer fee to
cover the refund inner.

methods.name: open

args.name: usdcPayment
args.desc: USDC asset transfer locking the maxPrice into escrow. sender == payerAddr, assetReceiver == app, xferAsset == usdcAssetId, assetAmount == maxPrice, fee == 0, and rekeyTo / assetCloseTo / assetSender all zero. The app must already be opted into USDC via init().

args.name: ticketId
args.desc: The unique identifier for the ticket. Must be 16 bytes in length.

args.name: operatorId
args.desc: The id of the operator serving this ticket. Must resolve to a registered, ACTIVE operator box.

args.name: nodeId
args.desc: The id of the serving node under operatorId. Must resolve to a registered, ACTIVE node box; that node's signing key must equal Txn.sender.

args.name: payerAddr
args.desc: The Algorand address that will be recorded as the ticket's payer and that must equal both funding txns' senders.

args.name: maxPrice
args.desc: The maximum USDC (microUSDC) escrowed for the ticket. Must equal usdcPayment.assetAmount. Under the additive fee model this is grossed up at reserve to cover the operator's base charge PLUS the protocol fee, so settlement can pay operator=amountCharged, treasury=netFee, and refund the rest to the payer. (The HAY fee discount is retired, so netFee equals the gross fee — there is no discount portion in the refund.)

args.name: expiresAt
args.desc: The unix timestamp (seconds) at which the ticket expires.

args.name: settlementGraceSeconds
args.desc: The number of grace seconds allowed for the ticket settlement. Defaults to the application-defined value if not provided or zero.

returns.desc: This method does not return a value but updates the application state with the new ticket record.

methods.desc:
Opens a new ticket with the specified parameters for a payment transaction.

The operator's owner and signing addresses are read from the
operator box (resolved by operatorId) and snapshotted into the
ticket — the payer cannot pass arbitrary addresses, and a
subsequent updateOperator does not retroactively redirect this
ticket's settlement.

Sender model: this method is a 2-tx group whose AppCall (this method)
is signed by the serving node's signing key (Txn.sender == nodeSigning).
The single funding txn (usdcPayment) is signed by the payer. The
operator's signature on the AppCall is consensus-verified at pool
admission, which binds them to the exact ABI args (operatorId,
maxPrice, expiresAt, payerAddr, ...). The contract additionally pins
the funding-txn sender to payerAddr so a third party can't co-opt the
ticket by substituting their own funding txn.

MBR model: the ticket-box MBR is no longer funded per-turn by a
payer-signed feePayment leg. The payer pre-deposited ALGO into their
per-payer pool (depositMbr → local state), and open() draws one box-MBR
slot against it: assert headroom, openTickets++. No ALGO moves here —
the deposit already raised app free balance and the new ticket box
consumes it. See proto/SPEC.md "Settlement asset model".

Fee model: fee responsibility shifts entirely to the operator. The
payer-signed usdcPayment carries fee=0; the node-signed AppCall
carries fee=2*minTxnFee, fee-pooling to cover both outer txns. There is
no settlement-inner-txn pre-fund — disbursements at settle time draw
from the settle group's outer fee pool instead.

methods.name: settle

args.name: ticketId
args.desc: - The unique identifier of the ticket to be settled.

args.name: amountCharged
args.desc: - The amount to be paid to the operator for the ticket.

args.name: receiptDigest
args.desc: - The 32-byte sha256("zs-receipt-v2\x00" || canonical_receipt_bytes) digest.

args.name: ttftMs
args.desc: - Operator-measured time-to-first-token (ms). On a non-stream / no-first-token settle this is the total service time and decodeMs is 0. Co-signed via the same match-or-freeze primitive as amountCharged (must match across both halves or the ticket freezes). On finalization it folds into the per-operator latency aggregates. The receipt digest commits to it too (see proto/SPEC.md "Receipt canonical bytes").

args.name: decodeMs
args.desc: - Operator-measured decode time (ms from first token to completion); 0 on non-stream / no-first-token settles. Co-signed via match-or-freeze. On finalization decodeMs + outputCount drive tokensPerSecEwma (only when outputUsageType==Tokens). Committed by the receipt digest.

args.name: inputCount
args.desc: - Operator-claimed actual input count (currently always tokens). Co-signed via match-or-freeze. On finalization it credits the operator's totalInputTokens and the protocol-wide aggregate. Committed by the receipt digest.

args.name: outputCount
args.desc: - Operator-claimed actual PRIMARY output count, in units of outputUsageType. Co-signed via match-or-freeze. On finalization it credits outputUnits[outputUsageType], the protocol-wide token aggregate (when type==Tokens), and (with decodeMs, when type==Tokens) the throughput EWMA. Committed by the receipt digest.

args.name: outputUsageType
args.desc: - UsageType of outputCount (1=Tokens, 2=Images, …). Co-signed via match-or-freeze. Selects the outputUnits slot and gates the latency/throughput EWMAs (folded only when ==Tokens). Must be < OUTPUT_UNITS_LEN. Committed by the receipt digest.

args.name: auxOutputUsageType
args.desc: - UsageType of the AUX output slot (Images on a text+image tool turn; None=0 otherwise). Co-signed via match-or-freeze. When != None, auxOutputCount additionally credits outputUnits[auxOutputUsageType]. Must be < OUTPUT_UNITS_LEN. Committed by the receipt digest.

args.name: auxOutputCount
args.desc: - Count for the AUX output slot (e.g. images produced by the zs_image_* tools alongside chat tokens). Co-signed via match-or-freeze. 0 when auxOutputUsageType == None. Committed by the receipt digest.

args.name: asOperator
args.desc: - true if the caller is acting as the operator side, false for the payer side. Must match the actual Txn.sender.

methods.desc:
Co-signed settle. Callable by either the serving node (node_signing only)
or the payer. The first call records a pending claim;
the second call must come from the other side.

If the second call's (amountCharged, receiptDigest) match the pending
claim, funds are released and the ticket box is deleted. If they
disagree, the ticket is frozen — the off-chain arbitration path can
inspect both sides' signed receipts.

If the payer never responds, the operator's pending claim can be
force-finalized after the deadline via settleLapsed.

Sender model: when called by the serving node's signing key, Algorand
consensus has already verified the per-txn Ed25519 signature at pool
admission — that bind operator-side authority to the exact
(amountCharged, receiptDigest) ABI args. When called by the payer,
the call is in a 2-txn group whose gtxn[0] is the operator's
pre-signed first-half (with consensus-verified args matching the
payer's gtxn[1] ack); the contract's match-check ensures the payer
cannot fabricate args. No in-contract ed25519verify here.

Caller role: the `asOperator` arg explicitly disambiguates which
side is calling (true = operator, false = payer). The contract
verifies Txn.sender matches the claimed role and dispatches the
pending-claim accounting accordingly. This is load-bearing in the
edge case where an operator uses their own signing account as a
payer (legal in this design — see open()): without the explicit
arg, the address-equality dispatch would silently treat both
halves of the atomic group as the same side and revert with a
confusing "same side" error.

Idempotent first-half: if status is already PENDING_SETTLE with the
SAME side as caller AND identical (amountCharged, receiptDigest),
this call is a no-op. This lets the atomic settle group
[op_first_half, payer_ack] succeed even when the operator's
settlement-driver watchdog has already fired a standalone first-half
with the same args. Mismatched args still revert.

Fee model: callers pay the disbursement inner-txn fees via outer
fee-pooling, and size that fee to the disbursements finalizeSettlement
will actually submit (each is gated independently below — see
finalizeSettlement). The atomic group's gtxn[0] (operator first-half)
carries fee = (2 outers + inners + gapOpUps) * minTxnFee: 5 on a paid
steady-state settle (USDC refund, operator payout, treasury fee), 2 on a
free model, which disburses nothing. The old ALGO MBR-refund inner is
gone, released via openTickets--. A standalone watchdog-fired settle
carries (1 outer + inners + one base op-up + gapOpUps) * minTxnFee; the
ack fires later from the other side with its own fee. settleLapsed is
sized the same way.

methods.name: settleLapsed

args.name: ticketId
args.desc: - The unique identifier of the ticket to be finalized.

methods.desc:
Force-finalizes a pending operator claim after the refund deadline has
passed and the payer has neither acknowledged nor protested. Callable by
anyone — the operator normally posts the tx, but a watcher bot can do it
instead if the operator is unavailable.

Only operator-initiated pending claims are eligible; a pending payer
claim with no operator counterpart goes through refundInactive instead.

methods.name: refundInactive

args.name: ticketId
args.desc: - The unique identifier of the ticket to be refunded.

methods.desc:
Payer escape hatch for a ticket that was never matched by an operator
claim. Legal when:
  - status is OPEN (no claim at all), or
  - status is PENDING_SETTLE but the pending side is the payer (operator
    never responded).
Tickets with an operator-side pending claim time out via settleLapsed,
not refundInactive, so the two paths are disjoint.

methods.name: protest

args.name: ticketId
args.desc: The unique identifier of the ticket being protested.

args.name: amountCharged
args.desc: The amount that was charged, which is being disputed in the protest.

args.name: receiptDigest
args.desc: The 32-byte sha256("zs-receipt-v2\x00" || canonical_receipt_bytes) digest of the node-signed receipt.

args.name: receiptSig
args.desc: The operator's 64-byte Ed25519 signature over receiptDigest. Verified against the ticket's nodeSigning.

args.name: disputeExcerpt
args.desc: A brief excerpt explaining the reason for the dispute.

args.name: reasonCode
args.desc: Payer-asserted protest reason (see proto/SPEC.md "Protest reason codes"). Must be non-zero. Not part of the receipt digest; carried as an indexable transaction arg for off-chain arbiters and analytics.

returns.desc: Does not return a value. Updates the state of the ticket persistently.

methods.desc:
Processes a ticket protest by validating the provided data, ensuring proper signature information,
and updating the ticket record to a frozen state if all conditions are met.

desc:
ZeroSignalEscrow — payment escrow contract for the ZeroSignal rollout.

Two control hats:
  - creator (Global.creatorAddress) gates updateApplication — bytecode control
  - admin (holder of adminTokenId ASA, 1-unit balance) gates runtime knobs (pause, config)

Operator / node identity: an OPERATOR is tracked by a monotonic uint64
id allocated by createOperator and is the economic entity — it holds the
cold `owner` payout address and the rolled-up metrics. An operator owns
many NODES (createNode), each a running endpoint with its own hot
`signing` key and `baseUrl`, keyed by the
compound box key (operatorId, nodeId) and carrying its own per-node
metrics. The owner can rotate the operator (updateOperator) or any node
(updateNode) without changing ids. Tickets snapshot the operator id, node
id, operator owner (payout), and the node's signing key at open() time so
in-flight settlement is deterministic regardless of subsequent rotation,
and so each settlement can bump both the serving node's box and the
operator rollup.

Operator authentication: `open` and `settle` rely on **consensus-verified
sender authentication** — the contract asserts `Txn.sender == nodeSigning`
(or, for the atomic settle group, `gtxn[0].sender == nodeSigning`),
which leverages Algorand's standard per-txn Ed25519 signature check at
pool admission time. This eliminates the in-contract `ed25519verify_bare`
(and its ~3 × min-fee OpUp pool) that those two methods previously called.
`protest()` keeps an in-contract `ed25519verify_bare` because it is the
payer's unilateral freeze primitive (no node-signed Algorand txn
available to gate it on); see protest() for the full rationale.

Why consensus-verified sender authentication is sufficient:

  1. Term-binding at open(). The operator pre-signs an Algorand
     ApplicationCall whose ABI args are the ticket's maxPrice / expiresAt /
     operatorId / payerAddr. The Algorand consensus signature on that txn
     body binds the operator to those exact values; the contract just
     reads them from the call args. A malicious payer cannot substitute
     different terms without invalidating the operator's signature.

  2. Squat-DoS protection at open(). ticketId becomes observable as soon
     as the open() group hits the mempool, but the operator's signed
     gtxn[1] is bound to a specific group hash that ties it to the
     proxy's specific funding txn. An attacker scraping the wire
     cannot rewrite the funding txn or reuse the operator's signature
     without forging Ed25519, same as before.

  3. Anti-fabrication on settle(). The first-half claim's
     (amountCharged, receiptDigest) are ABI args of an node-signed
     Algorand txn (gtxn[0] of the atomic group, or the operator's
     standalone watchdog settle). Algorand consensus binds those args
     to the serving node's signing key. A payer cannot fabricate first-half
     args; the only authority they have is to ack with matching args
     (gtxn[1] of the atomic group) or freeze via protest().

  4. Domain disjointness. For consensus-verified sites, this comes from
     ABI method-name disjointness (an `open()` AppCall txn cannot be
     mistaken for a `settle()` AppCall txn — different first-arg ABI
     selectors). For protest(), the existing "zs-receipt-v2\x00"
     digest tag continues to keep the receipt-sig domain separated from
     ticket signatures.

The off-chain ticket / receipt Ed25519 signatures (digest =
sha256(domain_tag || canonical_bytes)) are still produced by the
node for off-chain audit and for the receipt sig consumed by protest(),
but they are no longer the contract's primary verification surface for
open() / settle().

See proto/SPEC.md "Operator authentication" for the full design.

protoRevenueGross.desc: Σ amountCharged across every finalized settlement.

protoFeesNetCollected.desc: Σ netFee transferred to treasury over every finalized settlement — the gross fee after the HAY-tier discount. Under the additive fee model the fee is paid by the PAYER on top of the operator's base charge (their net cost = amountCharged + netFee); the operator's payout is the full amountCharged. The HAY-tier discount reduces this collected fee and is returned to the payer as a larger refund.

protoActiveTickets.desc: Count of ticket boxes currently alive on chain (OPEN+PENDING+FROZEN). Increments at open(), decrements only on box deletion (settle finalize, refundInactive). Freeze does NOT decrement — frozen funds are still in custody.

protoEscrowedUsdc.desc: Σ maxPrice locked in alive ticket boxes. Mirrors protoActiveTickets's increment/decrement sites — i.e. TVL of escrowed USDC in the app.

protoDiscountGrantedUsdc.desc: Σ (grossFee − netFee) over every finalized settlement — total USDC value forgone by the protocol due to fee discounts. DEPRECATED: the HAY fee discount is retired (discountBps is always 0), so netFee always equals grossFee and this accumulates 0. Kept for state-layout stability and a possible future discount mechanism.

protoTotalInputTokens.desc: Σ actual input tokens across every finalized settlement (clean + lapsed).

protoTotalOutputTokens.desc: Σ actual output tokens across every finalized settlement.
